post.caption: Kanazawa puts gold on ice cream. Soft serve topped with gold leaf is a specialty of Kanazawa, Japan, where nearly all of the country's gold leaf is made. The leaf is about a ten thousandth of a millimeter thick. Gold is mixed with a little silver and copper, rolled thin and cut into small squares, then beaten between sheets of special paper treated with persimmon juice and egg. Today a machine does the beating, about 700 strikes a minute. Kyoto's Golden Pavilion wears gold leaf on its top two floors, and in 1987 it was regilded with leaf about five times thicker than usual.
